name: peers_phonebook
description: peers with {"action": "phonebook"} must answer ok:true whatever the network looks like: a peer that is down is reported as status down inside the peers array, not surfaced as a tool failure, and no configured peers folds to an empty array. That makes the ok field the one environment-independent assertion — the eval is indifferent to how many peers exist or whether any answer. It goes red when the config read or the agent-card scan wiring breaks in a way that is neither an up nor a down entry.
prompt: Use the peers tool with input {"action": "phonebook"}. Look at the tool's JSON result and reply with only the value of its "ok" field: true or false. A result whose ok field is true still counts as true even if every listed peer has status down or the peers array is empty.
